$comment: Zoom-in on the single EC2 host: containers, networks, volumes, memory budget. Use when the hero diagram gets too crowded.

meta.title: Deployment Topology - inside the EC2 host

image_prompt: Draw a detailed container topology diagram, top to bottom, flat modern style. One large dashed rounded rectangle labelled 'AWS EC2 - Ubuntu, 8 GB RAM'. Inside it, a horizontal band labelled 'docker network: appnet (private bridge)'. Sitting on that band, five container boxes: 'cicd-edge (nginx)' at the top, with the ONLY arrow that crosses the host boundary out to the internet on port 80; below it two FastAPI containers 'rideiq-blue' and 'rideiq-green' side by side, blue outlined solid green and labelled ACTIVE, green greyed and labelled IDLE; then 'rideiq-redis'; then an orange 'rideiq-otp'. Draw a docker volume cylinder 'rideiq_data' attached to both FastAPI containers, and a host folder icon '/opt/rideiq/otp' attached to rideiq-otp. In one corner add a small stacked bar titled 'RAM budget of 8 GB' with segments labelled OTP 3.0, FastAPI x2 2.0, Redis 0.2, OS and Docker 1.0, headroom 1.8. Keep all text horizontal.

style.look: flat, modern, professional, whiteboard-clean, generous whitespace
style.shapes: rounded rectangles for services, cylinders for datastores, phone frame for client, dashed boundary for host/VM, hexagons for external data sources
style.typography: sans-serif; node titles bold, sublabels lighter and smaller; keep all text horizontal
rules: Never overlap arrows with node labels.
Solid arrows = live request traffic. Dashed arrows = build / deploy / data refresh.
Everything inside the dashed EC2 boundary lives on one physical host.

networks.name: appnet
networks.note: containers address each other by name; only nginx maps a host port

containers.name: cicd-edge
containers.note: config rewritten and reloaded on each deploy to point at the new colour

containers.name: rideiq-redis
containers.note: started once and never swapped by a deploy

containers.name: rideiq-otp
containers.note: eclipse-temurin:25-jre plus the OTP 2.9.0 shaded jar

annotations: During a deploy BOTH FastAPI colours run at once - that is the peak memory moment.
OTP is deliberately NOT blue-green: two JVMs each holding the graph will not fit in 8 GB.
A graph swap therefore costs about one minute of /transit returning 503. Nothing else is affected.
